background_story: Isaias was a young philosopher who spent most of his days pondering the mysteries of the universe. He was deeply fascinated by the works of Plato, often finding himself lost in the ancient Greek's philosophical dialogues. Isaias saw the world through the lens of Plato's Allegory of the Cave, believing that reality was merely a shadow of a higher, eternal realm. He spent years studying Plato's theory of forms, attempting to grasp the essence of justice, beauty, and goodness. As he delved deeper into Plato's philosophy, Isaias began to develop his own theories on the nature of reality and knowledge. His peers recognized him as a modern-day Platonic thinker, and his writings on the subject were met with critical acclaim. Isaias's love for Plato's philosophy had ignited a passion within him, driving him to contribute to the ongoing conversation about the human condition.
